items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: They wanted me to fire Charles Lloyd. ... These guys turned out to be young geniuses.

ctx.x: Yeah. You’re playing the room, right? That’s great. He also said something — oh he had a nice quote about you. He said, “Chico to me is in a sense like Duke Ellington. He plays his music using any player, any group of instruments. It doesn’t matter what it is he puts his own stamp on it.”

That’s true. That’s true. You know, being a band leader, or a leader of a group, it’s more than just having a name or creating a name or building a name. It’s being able to — knowing when to, how to present something. Knowing — I have an innate sense about well knowing talent, hearing talent, and seeing talent. And I know, see it takes two things, two very important things to reach a stage where you can make music, and that’s patience and fortitude. This I learned very early, in my early youth. So I had the…

that whatever talent that they might have, there’s always a resentment, a tremendous resentment when someone is different. I’ve been considered, okay I’m an innovator, I know that. Whether that’s good or bad or indifferent, but it’s a very lonely life, because you’re constantly — I’m past the stage of trying to please. I don’t please anybody. I play music for music’s sake. There should be no substitute for not playing your best, playing whatever you play. You play your best. And this is my whole thing, my whole…
